title: Advanced Optimizers & Regularization
description: Accelerate convergence beyond vanilla SGD using Momentum, RMSprop, Adam, and AdamW alongside modern regularization.

slides.title: The Evolution of Optimizers 🚀
slides.content:
# Moving Beyond Vanilla SGD

Vanilla Stochastic Gradient Descent struggles in ravines where surface curves much more steeply in one dimension than another. Modern optimizers adapt updates dynamically:

| Optimizer | Adaptive Mechanism | Primary Advantage | Typical Default Learning Rate |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **SGD + Momentum** | Accumulates exponential moving velocity vector | Powers through ravines and flat plateaus | $0.01 - 0.1$ |
| **RMSprop** | Divides updates by running root-mean-square of past gradients | Dampens oscillations in high-variance dimensions | $0.001$ |
| **Adam** | Combines Momentum (1st moment) with RMSprop (2nd moment) | Fast, robust default across NLP & Vision | $0.0003 - 0.001$ |
| **AdamW** | Decouples L2 weight decay from gradient update moments | State-of-the-art generalization for Transformers/LLMs | $0.0001 - 0.0005$ |

quizData.question: Which optimizer is widely considered the state-of-the-art standard for training modern Large Language Models and Transformers?

options.text: Vanilla Stochastic Gradient Descent without momentum

quizData.explanation: Loshchilov and Hutter demonstrated that standard Adam implements weight decay incorrectly when paired with momentum. AdamW fixes this decoupling and is the universal standard for modern foundation models.

slides.title: Deep Regularization: Dropout & Batch Normalization 🛡️
slides.content:
# Preventing Co-Adaptation

In deep networks with millions of parameters, individual neurons can become codependent on other specific neurons:

* **Dropout (Srivastava et al., 2014):** During training, randomly deactivates each neuron with probability $p$ (e.g. 20-50%). This forces the network to learn redundant, robust feature representations because no single neuron can be relied upon.
* **Batch Normalization (Ioffe & Szegedy, 2015):** Normalizes layer activations across the mini-batch to have zero mean and unit variance. This stabilizes internal covariate shift and enables significantly higher learning rates.

slides.title: Configuring AdamW and Dropout in PyTorch 🐍
slides.content: Configuring modern optimizers and regularization in PyTorch:
slides.codeSnippet:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

model = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Linear(784, 256),
    nn.BatchNorm1d(256),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Dropout(p=0.3),
    nn.Linear(256, 10)
)

# Configure AdamW with weight decay
optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3, weight_decay=1e-2)
print('Configured optimizer:', optimizer.__class__.__name__)
